question: How does a robot drive on Mars?
happened: A robot car called Perseverance is on Mars. This month it passed a driving record. It has rolled 28.10 miles. Most of the time it steers itself.

steps.title: Look
steps.text: The rover looks at the ground ahead.

steps.title: Choose
steps.text: It picks a safe path by itself.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Then it rolls along that path.

home.text: You do this too. You look at the floor and choose where to step. Then you walk. A rover does the same on Mars.

find_it.text: Mars is a planet far from Earth. Draw a rover rolling on it.

try_it.title: Be a rover
steps: Put three shoes on the floor with a grown-up.
Look closely. Choose a safe path around them.
Walk slowly along your path. Did you bump a shoe?

questions: What did you look at before you chose your path?
What might a rover need to look out for on Mars?
talk.tip: Today's skill is cause and effect: because the rover looks, it can choose a safe path. Ask "what happens next?" Don't correct; add one more detail.

next_week: Will the rover drive past 28.10 miles by next week? Guess, then check.
